correctness.rationale: The theorem quantifies over all integers b>=3,k>=1, ordered positive canonical base-b palindromes and exact gap b^k. For L(n)<=k, the digit-polynomial palindrome identity gives (X^a-1)D(X)=X^k-1, a=k-L+1, forcing a|k and the unique divisor-spaced digit pattern. For L(n)>k with equal length, the changed carry interval is reflection-invariant; any multi-position interval contradicts reflection of the old endpoint b-1, so L=2k+1 and exactly its middle digit increases, initially <=b-2. Length overflow creates leading 1 but retains final digit b-1, impossible for b>=3. The families are disjoint and give tau(k)+(b-1)^2*b^(k-1); k=1 and nonprime bases are included. Independently reimplemented bounded full pair enumeration for b=3..6 and k<=5 subject to computational grid, plus beyond-cutoff checks; no finite test is used for the unbounded quantifiers.

value.rationale: Pongsriiam and Saito explicitly ask about the finite counts associated with fixed palindrome gaps. Determining the exact number and every representing pair for all powers b^k across every nonbinary base addresses this precise natural invariant rather than a decorative small parameter. The divisor-spaced and fixed-middle-length decomposition explains why a finite gap family behaves uniformly.
